title: Recover one payment across lost responses
description: Model a client that intends one $42 payment. Move the response loss, change retry identity, and toggle atomic replay protection to see how network attempts become durable business effects.

failurePoints.label: Before the service receives it
failurePoints.detail: The network drops the request before validation or durable work begins.
failurePoints.clientObserved: No response; service created no charge

failurePoints.label: After validation, before commit
failurePoints.detail: The service saw the request but rolled back before creating the payment.

failurePoints.label: After commit, before response
failurePoints.detail: The payment exists, but the success response never reaches the client.
failurePoints.clientObserved: No response; one charge already committed

retryPolicies.label: Retry with the same key
retryPolicies.detail: Preserve one caller-scoped intent and the same normalized request fingerprint.

retryPolicies.label: Retry with a new key
retryPolicies.detail: Present every network attempt as a new business intent.

retryPolicies.label: Read status before another write
retryPolicies.detail: Look up the payment or operation by stable business reference before resubmitting.

replayStores.label: Atomic key, fingerprint, and result
replayStores.detail: The owner stores replay identity and durable outcome in the same correctness boundary.

replayStores.label: No replay record
replayStores.detail: The server cannot distinguish a retry from another valid payment request.
